The fourth, ElementFilterMember, is blocked on the expression layer, which is the next body of work and needs planning before any of it is written.
authored.next_step:
STOPPED BEFORE ElementFilterMember, deliberately. It is trivial in itself — `MemberPrefix 'filter' OwnedExpression ';'` — but its OwnedExpression slot is mandatory, and that is the whole expression layer. Unlike Import and AliasMember, whose frames accept real corpus input on their own, a filter frame without expressions accepts nothing real: all 22 filter statements in the pinned corpus carry an expression.
THE SCOPING, measured rather than estimated:
  - The expression layer is 157 productions (every rule under KerML clause 8.2.5.x), 28% of the grammar's 558 unique names.
  - OwnedExpression is an 8-way alternation: ConditionalExpression, ConditionalBinaryOperatorExpression, BinaryOperatorExpression, UnaryOperatorExpression, ClassificationExpression, MetaclassificationExpression, ExtentExpression, PrimaryExpression.
  - The 22 corpus filters: 13 are plain `@QualifiedName` (`filter @Safety;`, `filter @SysML::PartUsage;`), 5 add a binary operator (`filter @Safety or @Security;`, one using `|`), and 4 need a parenthesised cast and a feature chain (`filter @Safety and (as Safety).isMandatory;`). So even the cheapest useful slice reaches metadata access, type references and operator precedence.
  - NOTE the two pinned sources differ on the attribute: KerML 8.2.5.13 writes `condition = OwnedExpression`, SysML 8.2.2.5.1 writes `ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression`. Resolve that when implementing; it is a difference in what the element owns, not in what parses.
  - DO NOT use transitive closure size to scope grammar work here. OwnedExpression reaches 544 of 558 productions, but so do Package, Import and AliasMember, because RelationshipBody reaches OwnedAnnotation and PackageBody reaches DefinitionElement. The grammar is mutually recursive almost everywhere, so closure size is the same number for nearly every production and measures nothing. Count what the corpus actually exercises instead.
NEXT, in order:
  1. Plan the expression layer before writing any of it. Operator precedence is the part that cannot be retrofitted: a partial operator grammar built without it parses the easy cases and mis-associates the rest, and unpicking that later touches every expression production. .claude/scripts/ has add_precedence.py from the derivation work — start by reading what it already established. The derive-grammar skill is the six-phase workflow for this, and grammar_plan.py has never been run (grammar_next.py reports 'no units'), so the unit pipeline is available and unused.
  2. ElementFilterMember falls out cheaply once OwnedExpression exists. Leave it until then rather than shipping a frame that accepts nothing.
  3. OwnedAnnotation would let RelationshipBody accept real braced bodies, and would retire two rejection-by-absence cases. Independent of the expression layer and much smaller — a reasonable next increment if the expression layer is not being started yet.
  4. Only then point tests/corpus at vendor/corpus. Until it is wired the sweep's positive half claims nothing and says so on every run.
KNOWN GAPS in what exists:
  - Trivia attachment is positional, not owned, and the convention has not been decided. A graphical edit will care which node owns a comment.
  - parse_for_editor() from .claude/rules/syntax.md does not exist yet.
  - `sv2 parse` has no product on stdout: it is a check, not a dump.
  - Three rejection cases are rejections by absence rather than by rule, each naming what removes it: import-annotation-body-is-not-implemented and package-member-element-is-not-implemented.
  - cargo-insta is not installed, so a snapshot move needs manual promotion of each .snap.new with its reason, or a deliberate network install.

RESOLVED as far as it can be on one machine. The wikis are pinned by receipt: 1651 atoms in .claude/state/wiki-receipts.json, each with its clause, page, the wiki's region_sha256 to the source PDF span, and a file hash. Drift now fails the gate, and a citation naming a receipt that was never pinned now fails scripts/check_citations.py. NOT resolved: the wikis are not in the repository, because their 1651 atoms carry ~2.3 MB of verbatim OMG specification prose with no licence notice, and this repository is MIT and public. So a fresh clone can verify nothing until it builds its own wikis from the specification PDFs, which are not redistributable either. Revisit only if OMG's licensing changes, or if the wiki builder can be pinned and rerun from locally-held PDFs as part of a bootstrap.

pending_decisions.question: RESOLVED. regen_state.py recorded `git log --oneline -8` in the generated block and --check compared it, which has no fixed point: the commit carrying state.json cannot record its own hash, and amending only moves it. The gate was therefore red after every commit, for ever. Fixed by naming the compared measurements explicitly — COMPARED = (coverage, tests, pins) — and a pure is_stale() over them, with four tests including the one that says a new commit is not staleness. `commits` is still measured and written for whoever reads the block at session start; it is simply not evidence. Nothing else read it: not state_report.py, not the schema's required list. NOT weakened: coverage, tests and pins are still compared exactly as before, so an un-regenerated block after real work still fails.

How is the 157-production expression layer (KerML 8.2.5.x) approached? It is 28% of the grammar, it blocks ElementFilterMember and every construct with a value, and operator precedence is the part that cannot be retrofitted. Options: run the derive-grammar six-phase pipeline over the expression units, which is what it was built for and has never been used; or hand-implement by precedence tier from the pinned BNF, deriving precedence first. Either way, decide before writing any of it — a partial operator grammar parses the easy cases and mis-associates the rest, and unpicking that later touches every expression production.
